newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir guerrilla leader killed in shoot-out.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir guerrilla leader killed in shoot-out.

text.p: A senior leader of a Kashmiri separatist guerrilla group linked by Indian authorities to the kidnapping of four Western hostages was killed in a shoot-out involving security officers on Monday, police said.

"Arif Hussian Sheikh, supreme commander of banned Harkat-ul-Ansar militant outfit, was killed in crossfire during an encounter between the special operations group of Jammu and Kashmir police and militants when he was being taken for recovery of arms from a hideout," a police statement said.
Special operations group is the counter-insurgency wing of police in the state of Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority province. Srinagar is the state's summer capital.
Sheikh, also known as Abu Abdullah, was earlier arrested from Srinagar city area, the police statement said.
Harkat-ul-Ansar has neither confirmed nor denied the death of their leader.

Indian officials say shadowy Al-Faran guerrillas who kidnapped Britons Keith Mangan and Paul Wells, American Donald Hutchings and German Dirk Hasert in the Pahalgam region of Kashmir in July 1995 were members of Harkat-ul-Ansar.
Harkat-ul-Ansar, which favours the merger of Kashmir with neighbouring Pakistan, denies the charge.
The fate of the hostages is still unknown.

The body of a fifth hostage, Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe, was found beheaded in a Kashmir forest a month after the hostages were kidnapped. Another hostage, American John Childs, escaped to safety.

Police said militants fired on police when Sheikh was being taken to a guerrilla hideout to recover weapons. Sheikh was injured in the cross-fire between police and the militants, and later died in the hospital, the statement said.
In another incident suspected militants shot dead five members of a family on Sunday night about 80 km (50 mile) north of Srinagar, police said.
"During the preceding night, militants entered into the house of Mohammad Yusuf Mir...and resorted to indiscriminate firing," a police statement said.
About a dozen militant groups are fighting for Kashmir's independence or for merger with neighbouring Pakistan.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in the seven-year-old revolt in the Himalayan state.
